title: Clickable Detail Matrix
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Instructional Design; Learning Theory
description: Interactive HTML table generated from data.json that compares four invented learning theories across four dimensions. Cells are tinted by emphasis; clicking a cell opens a slide-in detail panel with a description and example, and a Random cell mode asks the learner to predict emphasis first.

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will differentiate several items across several dimensions by reading each cell's summary and then opening its explanation and example.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Comparison matrix with progressive disclosure and prediction
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Read summary, predict, open explanation and example
keyQuestions: On which dimension do two theories differ most?
Can you tell the theories apart from the summaries alone, without the color tints?
commonMisconceptions: Cells with similar summaries mean the same thing in every theory.
A color tint is enough to understand a cell without reading its explanation.
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the emphasis of unseen cells with a reason
Explain the difference between two theories on one dimension
